focus: Care Personally and Challenge Directly form the relationship base for candid management; trust is built by showing humanity while still saying what work and people need to hear.
coreClaim: Radical Candor is the combination of Care Personally and Challenge Directly, not a license for bluntness or a substitute for relationships.

centralConcept.name: two-axis trust
centralConcept.plainDefinition: Managerial trust forms when personal concern and direct challenge are present together. Either axis alone distorts feedback: warmth without challenge hides useful truth, and challenge without warmth feels like attack.
centralConcept.whyItMatters: A manager who internalizes the two-axis frame can diagnose a conversation by behavior, not by intention. The useful question becomes whether the other person received both care and clarity.

keyClaims: Care Personally treats employees as whole people rather than output machines.
Challenge Directly includes praise and criticism, so directness is not only negative feedback.
Radical Candor is a conversation compass, not a fixed label for someone's personality.
Robotic professionalism and managerial arrogance both weaken the relationship base.
The framework distinguishes direct kindness from brutal honesty.

namedExamples.label: Kim Scott at Google and Apple
namedExamples.summary: Kim Scott is documented as a former Google executive and former Apple executive whose management experiences supply the Silicon Valley setting for the framework. Kim Scott, Google AdSense, Apple executive role, and former Google executive are concrete anchors for the origin story rather than generic leadership scenery.
namedExamples.teachesWhat: A lived management setting keeps the relationship principle tied to observable workplace roles.

namedExamples.label: Sheryl Sandberg at Google
namedExamples.summary: Sheryl Sandberg is a real executive connected to Kim Scott's Google career, and public reporting describes Sandberg's management style as relying on human relationships at work. Sheryl Sandberg, Google, Facebook, and 2017 make the care-personally idea concrete.
namedExamples.teachesWhat: A senior leader can model whole-person openness without abandoning performance standards.

namedExamples.label: Care Personally plus Challenge Directly compass
namedExamples.summary: The official glossary places Care Personally at Ch. 1 pp. 12-13 and Challenge Directly at Ch. 1 pp. 9 and 14. Those page anchors make the two-axis relationship model a documented framework rather than a loose slogan.
namedExamples.teachesWhat: The two axes explain why kindness and clarity must arrive together.

hardEdge: The easy misread is to treat candor as blunt truth-telling with a warmer tone. The sharper point is relational: direct challenge lands differently only when the other person has real evidence of personal care.
voiceCues: uses a two-axis diagram as a memory tool
contrasts good intent with received impact
forbiddenLeakage: Do not import the full feedback order of operations from Relationships.
Do not use the seven-step GSD Wheel as the main structure.
paraphraseNotes: Care Personally and Challenge Directly create the base unit of the management philosophy. The Kim Scott career setting matters because the framework is not abstract etiquette; it comes from managing people in high-pressure technology organizations such as Google and Apple, with Google AdSense, Apple executive role, and former Google executive as visible operating-context details. Sheryl Sandberg provides a public model of whole-person leadership: public reporting describes her influence on a style that relies on human relationships and openness, while still operating inside demanding organizations. The official glossary gives the page anchors that make the two axes specific: Care Personally appears at Ch. 1 pp. 12-13, while Challenge Directly appears at Ch. 1 pp. 9 and 14. Use the compass as the local mechanism. Trust is not produced by friendliness alone, and directness is not proof of courage by itself. A manager can be warm and still deprive someone of useful information, or be accurate and still damage the relationship by failing to show care. Keep the emphasis on received behavior: the team member must be able to see both personal concern and a willingness to name reality.

testableFacts.claim: Care Personally is documented at Ch. 1 pp. 12-13 as the whole-person side of the trust model.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Because whole-person concern lowers defensiveness, direct guidance is more likely to be heard as help.
testableFacts.commonError: Assuming professionalism requires leaving personal realities outside work.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: That misses the stated antidote to robotic professionalism.

testableFacts.claim: Challenge Directly is documented at Ch. 1 pp. 9 and 14 as naming both good work and work that is not good enough.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Since directness covers praise and criticism, the standard is clarity rather than negativity.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: That hides the role of specific praise in reinforcing high standards.

testableFacts.claim: Radical Candor combines Care Personally and Challenge Directly at the same time.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Because either axis alone distorts the conversation, the useful behavior is the combination.
testableFacts.commonError: Choosing either kindness or honesty as the manager's style.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: The framework requires both in the same interaction.

testableFacts.claim: Kim Scott's public biography connects the framework to Google, Apple, and AdSense management settings.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Because those settings involve real teams and products, the idea is grounded in operating roles rather than etiquette theory.
testableFacts.commonError: Reading the framework as generic manners advice.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: The source context is management under workplace pressure.

testableFacts.claim: Sheryl Sandberg's Google and Facebook leadership is used as a public example of bringing humanity to work.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Because visible vulnerability can reduce awkward silence, teams can return to hard business questions with less pretending.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: The public example pairs openness with demanding work.

testableFacts.claim: The official basics page separates Radical Candor from brutal honesty.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Because care changes how directness is received, the same factual statement can either help or harm.
testableFacts.commonError: Using the phrase as cover for harsh delivery.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: Brutal delivery lacks the personal-care axis.

testableFacts.claim: The compass is used for conversations rather than personality typing.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Since a person can move among quadrants by behavior, the tool diagnoses moments instead of branding people.
testableFacts.commonError: Labeling a colleague as permanently candid or aggressive.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: That turns a behavioral guide into a fixed identity claim.

testableFacts.claim: Care Personally can be as small as acknowledging a bad day and making space for others to do the same.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Because small disclosures signal humanity, they create permission for honest work conversations.
testableFacts.commonError: Waiting for dramatic personal disclosure before showing care.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: The mechanism works through ordinary signals.

testableFacts.claim: Challenge Directly means sharing humble opinions, not claiming ownership of the truth.
testableFacts.becauseMechanism: Because humility leaves room for correction, direct challenge can start dialogue instead of closing it.
testableFacts.errorIsWhy: The model frames challenge as a candid view offered with openness.
